deep.reconstruction:
The page holds two lists of quadratic residues, written in the same format as the neighbouring pages (491, 499, 503 before; 983, 977 after). Each block has a prime p in the margin and a '+' sign (meaning 'residues'), followed by an increasing list of integers a with Legendre symbol (a/p) = +1.

(1) p = 997. Since 997 ≡ 1 (mod 4), (-1/997) = +1, so a and p−a have the same character. Gauss therefore lists only 1 ≤ a ≤ (p−1)/2 = 498. The list runs 1, 3, 4, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14, 16, 19, … and ends at 496. It should contain exactly 249 numbers. This matches the convention on the next page, where p = 977 ≡ 1 (mod 4) is listed only up to 488.

(2) p = 991. Since 991 ≡ 3 (mod 4), (-1/991) = −1 and the list is not symmetric. Gauss therefore lists the residues over the whole range 1 ≤ a ≤ 990, which should be 495 numbers. The list runs 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 13, … and ends at 988. The previous-page tables for 491, 499 and 503 follow the same convention: those primes are all ≡ 3 (mod 4) and are listed beyond (p−1)/2.

There is no derivation on the page. The lists are presumably built from squares mod p, or from the multiplicativity of the character applied to primes. My spot checks with quadratic reciprocity agree with the entries:
- For 997 (≡ 5 mod 8): 2 is absent, 3 present, 5, 7, 11, 17 absent; 13, 19, 23 present; 29 absent; 30, 31 present.
- For 991 (≡ 7 mod 8): 2 and 5 present; 3, 7, 11 absent; 13 present.

Several entries are corrections:
- Superscript insertions over a blot: 258, 259, 264, 268 in the 997 list and 416 in the 991 list. All of these are genuine residues, as reciprocity confirms.
- Blots in the 991 list after 36, 180, 512 and 699 cover no residues: 37 and 181–186, and 513–516 and 700–704, are all non-residues. So these blots are deletions of erroneous entries.
- The blot after 316 in the 991 list must contain 317, because (317/991) = (991/317) = (40/317) = (2/317)^3 (5/317) = (−1)(−1) = +1.

Purpose: these are working auxiliary tables of quadratic residues for primes near 500 and 1000. Gauss used such tables for questions on residue distribution, class numbers and quadratic forms, and for factorisation by the exclusion method (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae, art. 319 ff.).
errors: No arithmetic errors found in the spot checks. The corrections Gauss made are themselves correct: the inserted 258, 259, 264, 268 (p = 997) and 416 (p = 991) are residues. The blotted deletions at 991 after 36, 180, 512 and 699 remove entries in ranges containing no residues.
